summary: Milestone 2026.05.266 was planned but no experiments were dispatched in the timing window. The outer-loop research planning session staged a 10-task roadmap (exp2809-exp2818) targeting pre-test cascade repair, multi-corpus FoVer overfit evaluation, and FUSE zero-label verifier ensemble composition. This is the forty-first consecutive empty-timing-window retro; experiments_completed=0 is a timing-script infrastructure gap, not a research failure.
bottlenecks_identified: Timing-script look-back is not anchored to conductor-state.json activated_at, causing every retro to report 0 experiments completed regardless of actual milestone output. This has persisted for 41+ consecutive milestones.

Three consecutive milestones (.263, .264, .265) were entirely blocked by a pre-test cascade (PySAT import error + missing KV260 Verilog stub + docs assertion). The .266 roadmap correctly gates 9 of 10 tasks on exp2810 pretest_cascade_fixed=true, making the cascade fix the critical path.

No compute-bound tasks ran this milestone; gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks=null. GPU idle is NOT a bottleneck here — this is correct behaviour for a planning-only milestone with no GGUF/CUDA code path.
improvements_suggested: Fix timing-script look-back to use conductor-state.json activated_at as the left boundary of the timing window. This is the root cause of 41 consecutive empty-window retros.
Add a pre-retro health check: conductor emits WARNING and blocks retro generation if experiments_completed == 0 AND milestone_age_minutes > 60, prompting operator review before retro fires.

Merge the three failing pre-test root causes (PySAT import, discrete_sb_256_tb.v stub, docs assertion) into a single exp2810 atomic fix with all-three-must-pass acceptance gate, rather than fixing them separately across milestones — this avoids partial-fix re-cascade.

Stage a milestone-activation sentinel commit (empty commit message '[conductor] milestone N activated') at task-dispatch start, providing a deterministic timing boundary independent of the look-back script.
Consider a DualGPURunner engagement check: if 2+ GGUF models are loaded in exp2811-exp2814 (multi-corpus evaluation tasks), verify DualGPURunner is invoked rather than sequential single-GPU loading.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix timing-script look-back to conductor-state.json activated_at anchor — eliminates the 41-milestone recurring empty-window retro pattern with a single code change in scripts/research_conductor.py (BLOCKED per task instructions: do not modify research_conductor.py this turn; queue for next outer-loop session).

Prioritize exp2810 pre-test cascade fix v4 as the first dispatched task in .266 — three consecutive zero-artifact milestones (.263, .264, .265) represent ~30 experiment-slots of lost research capacity; a successful fix unblocks 9 of 10 remaining .266 tasks immediately.

Add a pre-retro empty-milestone alert: if experiments_completed == 0 at retro generation time and milestone_age_hours > 1, emit a conductor WARNING that halts retro and surfaces the gap to the operator before wall-time is consumed by downstream planning cycles.
meta_reflection: Three consecutive milestones lost to a pre-test cascade (.263, .264, .265) demonstrate that a single unchecked failing test can deadlock an entire milestone when the fix task is inside the blocked milestone. The .266 roadmap correctly addresses this by structuring exp2810 as a dependency-bearing outer-loop fix (requires_claude: true, max_turns: 100) rather than a gemini experiment task. The recurring 41-milestone empty-timing-window pattern is now the highest-priority infrastructure gap — it obscures real milestone throughput data and makes operational retrospectives structurally unreliable.
